depthDefinitions.worked-example: This concept has a direct worked example in an authored guide; not a claim of API completeness or mastery.
depthDefinitions.reference: Original definition and linked guide/resources; dedicated examples and assessments still need expansion.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: TypeScript checks relationships between values before execution; the emitted JavaScript still needs runtime validation.

concepts.title: Types
concepts.definition: Types describe permitted values and operations. Prefer precise domain types to pervasive any.

concepts.title: Interfaces
concepts.definition: Interfaces describe structural shapes and can support declaration merging.

concepts.title: Type aliases
concepts.definition: Aliases name type expressions such as unions, tuples, and mapped types.

concepts.title: Unions
concepts.definition: A union permits one of several alternatives; discriminate valid application states with a stable field.

concepts.title: Intersections
concepts.definition: An intersection requires the combined constraints of multiple types; incompatible members can produce impossible types.

concepts.title: Generics
concepts.definition: Generics preserve a relationship between inputs and outputs rather than discarding information through any.

concepts.title: Utility types
concepts.definition: Utilities such as Pick, Omit, Partial, and Record transform type structure; they do not validate data.

concepts.title: Narrowing
concepts.definition: Control-flow analysis refines a type after checks such as typeof or a discriminant test.

concepts.title: Type guards
concepts.definition: A guard claims a runtime check establishes a type; an incorrect guard can create false confidence.

concepts.title: Enums
concepts.definition: Enums can emit runtime objects; literal unions are often enough when only a compile-time set is required.

concepts.title: Modules
concepts.definition: Explicit imports and exports coordinate types and values; type-only imports avoid unnecessary runtime dependencies.

concepts.title: Classes
concepts.definition: Access modifiers and implements help model intent; static type constraints are not a substitute for runtime authority.

concepts.title: Advanced types
concepts.definition: Conditional, mapped, indexed-access, and template-literal types express complex relationships at a readability cost.

concepts.title: TypeScript with React
concepts.definition: Type props, events, and state according to their actual roles; unions can prevent conflicting request states.

concepts.title: TypeScript with Node
concepts.definition: Match compiler module settings to Node's runtime package and import rules.

concepts.title: TypeScript with Express
concepts.definition: Type checked service inputs after validating the request; request generics alone do not authenticate a payload.

concepts.title: Full-stack TypeScript
concepts.definition: Share domain contracts while preserving server-owned fields and independent runtime boundary validation.

concepts.title: Git fundamentals
concepts.definition: Commits identify snapshots and parent relationships; the working tree and staging area represent different states.

concepts.title: Branching
concepts.definition: A branch is a movable name pointing to a commit, not a separate copy of every file.

concepts.title: Merging
concepts.definition: A merge combines histories, potentially creating a commit with multiple parents.

concepts.title: Rebasing
concepts.definition: Rebase replays commits onto a new base and changes their identities; coordinate before rewriting shared history.

concepts.title: Stashing
concepts.definition: Stash stores selected work temporarily; understand whether untracked files are included and verify restoration.

concepts.title: Cherry-pick
concepts.definition: Cherry-pick applies a commit's change on another history and normally creates a new commit identity.

concepts.title: Reset
concepts.definition: Reset moves a reference and can alter the index or working tree depending on mode; inspect before using destructive modes.

concepts.title: Revert
concepts.definition: Revert creates a new commit that reverses an earlier change while retaining shared history.

concepts.title: Git workflows
concepts.definition: A workflow defines branches, review, checks, and release decisions; choose it for the team rather than fashion.

concepts.title: Pull requests
concepts.definition: A pull request proposes a branch difference for review and collaboration.

concepts.title: Code review
concepts.definition: Review checks behavior, maintainability, evidence, security boundaries, and scope rather than only formatting.

concepts.title: GitHub Actions
concepts.definition: Workflows run configured jobs on events; least-privilege permissions and untrusted-input handling matter.

concepts.title: Open-source contribution
concepts.definition: Read contribution rules, preserve provenance, describe the change, and supply reproducible verification.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: React describes interfaces as components whose output depends on inputs and state.

concepts.title: JSX
concepts.definition: JSX describes element structure and is transformed before execution; it is not an HTML string.

concepts.title: Components
concepts.definition: Components encapsulate presentation and behavior; keep rendering pure so repeated evaluation remains safe.

concepts.title: Props
concepts.definition: Props are inputs from a parent and should not be mutated by the receiving component.

concepts.title: State
concepts.definition: State records facts the component owns. Derive values that can be computed from existing facts.

concepts.title: Events
concepts.definition: Event handlers express user intent and can trigger state changes or commands.

concepts.title: Forms
concepts.definition: Form state, validation, submission, and recovery need distinct behavior; preserve drafts when requests fail.

concepts.title: Conditional rendering
concepts.definition: Render a clear representation for each valid state, including loading, empty, error, and success.

concepts.title: Lists
concepts.definition: Transform data into elements without changing item identity as order changes.

concepts.title: Keys
concepts.definition: Stable keys let React identify siblings across updates; random or index-based keys can lose the correct local state.

concepts.title: Hooks
concepts.definition: Hooks connect React capabilities to function components under ordering rules.

concepts.title: useState
concepts.definition: useState provides a state snapshot and update function; functional updates compose against previous state.

concepts.title: useEffect
concepts.definition: Effects synchronize with external systems and need correct dependencies and cleanup.

concepts.title: useRef
concepts.definition: A ref persists a mutable value without scheduling rendering; do not use it to conceal missing UI state.

concepts.title: useMemo
concepts.definition: Memoization can avoid recomputation when dependencies are equal; measure benefit and avoid relying on cache for correctness.

concepts.title: useCallback
concepts.definition: A cached function identity can help specific memoized boundaries; it is not a general speed switch.

concepts.title: useContext
concepts.definition: Context passes a value through a subtree; changing that value can affect consuming components.

concepts.title: Custom hooks
concepts.definition: A custom hook reuses stateful logic while each caller has its own hook state unless an external store is used.

concepts.title: Component architecture
concepts.definition: Separate reusable presentation, domain state, and external communication where this simplifies change.

concepts.title: Routing
concepts.definition: Routing maps location to views and defines navigation, parameters, and loading boundaries.

concepts.title: React Router
concepts.definition: React Router offers modes with different routing and data behavior; choose a mode deliberately and consult its matching docs.

concepts.title: Data fetching
concepts.definition: Associate responses with request identity and model caching, invalidation, cancellation, and errors.

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.definition: Distinguish render errors, rejected asynchronous work, validation failures, and conflict recovery.

concepts.title: Performance
concepts.definition: Profile actual interaction; list size, expensive work, and network waterfalls often matter more than blanket memoization.

concepts.title: Lazy loading
concepts.definition: Load code for a boundary when needed, then provide loading and failure behavior for that boundary.

concepts.title: Suspense
concepts.definition: Suspense coordinates supported pending resources; arbitrary effect-based fetching does not automatically integrate with it.

concepts.title: Server/client concepts
concepts.definition: Server and client components have different capabilities and bundle boundaries supplied by a compatible framework.

concepts.title: Testing
concepts.definition: Test visible behavior and accessible interaction, then run important workflows in a real browser.

concepts.title: Accessibility
concepts.definition: Use native roles, labels, focus management, and keyboard behavior through state transitions.

concepts.title: Production architecture
concepts.definition: Define data ownership, request contracts, error recovery, bundle boundaries, and operating evidence before multiplying abstractions.

concepts.title: Local state
concepts.definition: Keep a fact near its users until a real sharing requirement appears.

concepts.title: Context
concepts.definition: Context transports a shared value through a subtree; it does not automatically manage remote caching or normalize entities.

concepts.title: Redux
concepts.definition: Redux centralizes predictable transitions through actions and reducers; it has an ecosystem for complex shared application state.

concepts.title: Redux Toolkit
concepts.definition: Redux Toolkit provides the recommended Redux setup and utilities, reducing hand-written store boilerplate.

concepts.title: Zustand
concepts.definition: Zustand provides an external store with selectors; subscriptions and ownership still need intentional design.

concepts.title: Server state
concepts.definition: Server state has remote authority, freshness, invalidation, and concurrent-writer concerns beyond local component state.

concepts.title: TanStack Query
concepts.definition: TanStack Query coordinates asynchronous server-state caching and lifecycle; query keys and invalidation define correctness.

concepts.title: When to use which approach
concepts.definition: Choose local state, context, an external store, or a query cache according to ownership and coordination needs.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: Next.js supplies routing, rendering, and server integration around React; match documentation to the installed version and router.

concepts.title: Routing
concepts.definition: File conventions map URLs to pages, layouts, loading states, and handlers; parameters still need validation.

concepts.title: Layouts
concepts.definition: Layouts wrap route segments and can persist across navigation; do not assume every navigation remounts them.

concepts.title: Server Components
concepts.definition: Server Components can read server resources without sending their implementation to the client bundle.

concepts.title: Client Components
concepts.definition: Client boundaries enable interactive hooks and browser capabilities; their imported client dependency graph affects the bundle.

concepts.title: Data fetching
concepts.definition: Choose server or client fetching according to authority, latency, and interaction; define freshness explicitly.

concepts.title: Server Actions
concepts.definition: Server Actions execute server functions through framework transport and still require input validation and authorization.

concepts.title: API routes
concepts.definition: App Router Route Handlers expose HTTP methods; Pages Router API routes use a different convention.

concepts.title: Middleware
concepts.definition: In Next.js 16, the middleware file convention is deprecated in favor of proxy; it is distinct from Express middleware.

concepts.title: Authentication
concepts.definition: Resolve trusted identity and enforce resource authorization at the data or operation boundary, including actions and handlers.

concepts.title: Caching
concepts.definition: Caching behavior is version-sensitive; use explicit cache and revalidation choices rather than historical default assumptions.

concepts.title: Rendering strategies
concepts.definition: Choose when and where content is rendered based on personalized data, freshness, and distribution needs.

concepts.title: Static rendering
concepts.definition: Precomputed content can be distributed cheaply when its inputs and invalidation rules permit it.

concepts.title: Dynamic rendering
concepts.definition: Request-dependent content must preserve per-request identity and avoid unsafe shared caching.

concepts.title: Streaming
concepts.definition: Streaming sends ready portions before the whole response finishes; boundaries affect loading and error behavior.

concepts.title: Deployment
concepts.definition: Hosting must support the selected server features; a static export cannot provide arbitrary dynamic server behavior.

concepts.title: Performance
concepts.definition: Measure bundle size, waterfalls, caching, and useful rendered content before changing rendering strategy.

concepts.title: Internet fundamentals
concepts.definition: The Internet connects networks. The Web uses that infrastructure to exchange resources identified by URLs.

concepts.title: How the Web works
concepts.definition: A browser requests resources, interprets HTML and CSS, runs scripts, and sends later application requests.

concepts.title: Browser architecture
concepts.definition: Browser processes separate responsibilities such as rendering, networking, and isolation; their implementation varies by browser.

concepts.title: HTTP/HTTPS
concepts.definition: HTTP defines request and response semantics. HTTPS carries HTTP over an authenticated, encrypted TLS connection.

concepts.title: DNS
concepts.definition: DNS resolves names into records used to locate services. DNS resolution and HTTP caching have different lifetimes.

concepts.title: TCP/IP basics
concepts.definition: IP routes packets; TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream. HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP instead of TCP.

concepts.title: APIs
concepts.definition: An API is a contract between software components. A web API exposes a network-accessible contract.

concepts.title: JSON
concepts.definition: JSON encodes data values, not functions or every JavaScript type. Dates and domain types need explicit conventions.

concepts.title: Client-server architecture
concepts.definition: The client presents interaction; the server validates requests and owns trusted business decisions.

concepts.title: Developer tools
concepts.definition: Network, console, debugger, performance, and accessibility tools expose evidence about browser behavior.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: Elements express document structure; attributes refine meaning and behavior. A valid document has a declared language and useful title.

concepts.title: Semantic HTML
concepts.definition: Use headings, landmarks, lists, links, and buttons for their meaning and built-in interaction.

concepts.title: Forms
concepts.definition: Labels, names, input types, constraints, and submit behavior form a usable contract; the server validates again.

concepts.title: Tables
concepts.definition: Tables express relationships in rows and columns. Captions and header associations help users interpret the data.

concepts.title: Multimedia
concepts.definition: Images, audio, and video need alternatives appropriate to their purpose, including captions or transcripts when needed.

concepts.title: Accessibility
concepts.definition: Accessibility includes keyboard interaction, names, focus, structure, contrast, and assistive-technology behavior.

concepts.title: SEO
concepts.definition: Descriptive titles, useful content, crawlable links, and meaningful structure help discovery; metadata is not a ranking guarantee.

concepts.title: HTML APIs
concepts.definition: Browser APIs such as dialog, history, and storage have specific lifecycle and permission contracts beyond markup.

concepts.title: Modern HTML
concepts.definition: Native dialog, disclosure, responsive images, and newer platform features can reduce custom code; check support for your audience.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: CSS maps selectors to declarations; browsers resolve competing declarations and compute values for elements.

concepts.title: Box model
concepts.definition: Content, padding, border, and margin determine geometry. border-box includes padding and borders in the declared width.

concepts.title: Selectors
concepts.definition: Selectors match document structure and states; prefer intentional classes over tightly coupled ancestor chains.

concepts.title: Cascade
concepts.definition: Origin, importance, layers, specificity, scope proximity, and order resolve competing declarations.

concepts.title: Specificity
concepts.definition: Specificity compares selector weight within the relevant cascade stage; it is not the first rule in every conflict.

concepts.title: Flexbox
concepts.definition: Flexbox distributes items along an axis and manages wrapping, alignment, and available space.

concepts.title: Grid
concepts.definition: Grid defines tracks in two dimensions and can coordinate row and column placement.

concepts.title: Responsive design
concepts.definition: A responsive layout adapts to available space, input capabilities, text size, and content length.

concepts.title: Media queries
concepts.definition: Media queries condition rules on viewport or device characteristics; choose breakpoints from content needs.

concepts.title: Animations
concepts.definition: Keyframe animations interpolate properties over time; honor reduced-motion preferences and avoid unnecessary layout work.

concepts.title: Transitions
concepts.definition: Transitions interpolate a changed property over a duration; they need distinct before and after values.

concepts.title: Positioning
concepts.definition: Static, relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky positioning use different containing-block and scroll relationships.

concepts.title: Variables
concepts.definition: Custom properties cascade and can be resolved at use time; they are useful for design tokens and themes.

concepts.title: Accessibility
concepts.definition: Preserve readable contrast, focus, zoom, reduced motion, and logical source order.

concepts.title: Modern CSS
concepts.definition: Container queries, cascade layers, subgrid, logical properties, and modern selectors solve specific layout problems; inspect compatibility.

concepts.title: CSS architecture
concepts.definition: Small reusable patterns, consistent naming, and documented tokens reduce unintended cross-component effects.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: JavaScript evaluates expressions and statements using a language-defined value model and host-provided APIs.

concepts.title: Variables
concepts.definition: Bindings associate names with values; const prevents reassignment of a binding, not mutation of its object.

concepts.title: Data types
concepts.definition: Primitives and objects have different identity behavior. undefined, null, numbers, strings, booleans, bigint, and symbols need explicit handling.

concepts.title: Operators
concepts.definition: Operators combine or compare values; coercion, short-circuiting, and nullish behavior affect results.

concepts.title: Control flow
concepts.definition: Conditions, loops, return, break, and continue select which work runs and when iteration ends.

concepts.title: Functions
concepts.definition: Functions define callable behavior, parameters, return values, and closures over lexical bindings.

concepts.title: Scope
concepts.definition: Lexical scope resolves names from where code is written, not from whichever function called it.

concepts.title: Closures
concepts.definition: A function retains access to its lexical environment, including bindings whose values can change.

concepts.title: Hoisting
concepts.definition: Declarations are instantiated before evaluation, but initialization timing differs; let and const have a temporal dead zone.

concepts.title: this
concepts.definition: Ordinary function this depends on invocation; arrows capture the surrounding this and cannot be rebound with call.

concepts.title: Objects
concepts.definition: Objects group properties and have identity; spreading creates a shallow copy of own enumerable properties.

concepts.title: Arrays
concepts.definition: Arrays hold indexed collections; map transforms, filter selects, and reduce accumulates values.

concepts.title: Destructuring
concepts.definition: Destructuring binds values from structured data; defaults apply to undefined rather than every falsy value.

concepts.title: Spread/rest
concepts.definition: Spread expands values; rest collects remaining arguments or properties. Object spread does not deeply clone nested objects.

concepts.title: Prototypes
concepts.definition: Property lookup can follow a prototype chain after own properties are checked.

concepts.title: Classes
concepts.definition: Classes provide syntax around constructors and prototype-based methods, with additional class-specific semantics.

concepts.title: Inheritance
concepts.definition: Inheritance reuses behavior through type or prototype relationships; composition can avoid rigid hierarchies.

concepts.title: Modules
concepts.definition: Modules make dependencies and exports explicit; ESM and CommonJS have different loading and interoperability rules.

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.definition: Throw, try/catch, and Promise rejection represent failures; handle errors at a boundary that can act.

concepts.title: Memory
concepts.definition: Retained references determine whether objects remain reachable; caches, listeners, and closures can retain large graphs.

concepts.title: Garbage collection
concepts.definition: The engine reclaims unreachable objects; collection timing is not a portable application guarantee.

concepts.title: Iterators
concepts.definition: An iterator returns successive value/done results; iterable protocols allow for-of and spread to consume sequences.

concepts.title: Generators
concepts.definition: Generators suspend and resume function execution while yielding values, providing convenient iterator state.

concepts.title: Symbols
concepts.definition: Symbols create distinct property keys and participate in protocols such as iteration.

concepts.title: Proxy
concepts.definition: A Proxy intercepts operations on a target through traps; language invariants constrain permitted behavior.

concepts.title: Reflect
concepts.definition: Reflect exposes operations corresponding to object internal behavior and can preserve forwarding semantics in traps.

concepts.title: Typed arrays
concepts.definition: Typed arrays view fixed-format binary values in buffers; byte layout and bounds matter.

concepts.title: Internationalization
concepts.definition: Intl formats numbers, dates, and text according to locale conventions; formatting is separate from domain storage.

concepts.title: Modern ECMAScript
concepts.definition: Language additions vary by runtime support. Check the target runtime rather than assuming a proposal is standardized.

concepts.title: TC39 proposals
concepts.definition: Proposals have explicit stages and can change or stop progressing; inspect proposal status and runtime support before relying on experimental behavior.

concepts.title: Performance
concepts.definition: Measure workload, allocation, and blocking time before replacing readable code with an optimization.

concepts.title: Security
concepts.definition: Treat untrusted values as data; validate at boundaries and avoid executing input or inserting it as HTML.

concepts.title: Callbacks
concepts.definition: A callback is a function another operation invokes; it can run synchronously or asynchronously according to that contract.

concepts.title: Promises
concepts.definition: A Promise represents an eventual outcome. Chaining transforms outcomes and propagates failures.

concepts.title: async/await
concepts.definition: An async function returns a Promise; await suspends that function until the awaited outcome is available.

concepts.title: Event loop
concepts.definition: A host coordinates execution and queued work. Browser rendering and Node phases have distinct scheduling models.

concepts.title: Microtasks
concepts.definition: Promise reactions and queueMicrotask callbacks run at host-defined checkpoints after the current work.

concepts.title: Macrotasks
concepts.definition: Task is the browser-standard term; timers and other task sources schedule later work with no exact execution-time guarantee.

concepts.title: Fetch
concepts.definition: Fetch produces an HTTP response or transport failure; the application still checks status and parses the expected representation.

concepts.title: Async programming
concepts.definition: Design ordering, cancellation, concurrency limits, timeouts, and partial-failure behavior explicitly.

concepts.title: DOM
concepts.definition: The DOM exposes a document tree as objects that scripts can inspect and update.

concepts.title: Events
concepts.definition: Events describe interaction or state changes; propagation and default actions follow distinct rules.

concepts.title: Browser APIs
concepts.definition: Storage, history, observers, workers, and permissions have host-specific contracts and cleanup requirements.

concepts.title: Forms and events
concepts.definition: A submit event captures keyboard and button submission; form controls should retain accessible names and feedback.

concepts.title: Runtime fundamentals
concepts.definition: Node executes JavaScript with host capabilities such as files, networking, and processes rather than a browser DOM.

concepts.title: V8
concepts.definition: V8 parses and executes JavaScript and manages memory; Node combines it with other runtime components.

concepts.title: Modules
concepts.definition: Modules define explicit dependency boundaries; loading behavior depends on ESM or CommonJS configuration.

concepts.title: CommonJS
concepts.definition: CommonJS uses require and module.exports with its own loading and interoperability behavior.

concepts.title: ESM
concepts.definition: ESM uses import and export; package type and extensions affect how Node interprets files.

concepts.title: npm
concepts.definition: npm manages package metadata and dependency installation; a lockfile makes the chosen graph reproducible.

concepts.title: package.json
concepts.definition: The manifest defines scripts, module type, dependency ranges, and supported runtime expectations.

concepts.title: File system
concepts.definition: Filesystem APIs operate on paths and data; prefer asynchronous work in request handlers and constrain user-influenced paths.

concepts.title: Events
concepts.definition: Runtime events announce lifecycle changes; handle required error events and remove unnecessary listeners.

concepts.title: EventEmitter
concepts.definition: EventEmitter invokes registered listeners according to its contract; asynchronous listener failures require deliberate handling.

concepts.title: Buffers
concepts.definition: Buffers represent binary bytes rather than Unicode text and require explicit encoding decisions.

concepts.title: Streams
concepts.definition: Streams process data incrementally; backpressure prevents producers from overwhelming consumers.

concepts.title: HTTP
concepts.definition: Node exposes request and response primitives, while a framework can organize validation and routing above them.

concepts.title: Networking
concepts.definition: Sockets and connection pools consume finite resources; timeouts and lifecycle cleanup matter.

concepts.title: Process
concepts.definition: The process has signals, exit status, resources, and environment; shutdown must account for in-flight work.

concepts.title: Environment variables
concepts.definition: Environment variables configure deployment; parse required values at startup and keep secrets out of logs.

concepts.title: Child processes
concepts.definition: Child processes run separate programs; avoid interpolating untrusted data into shell command strings.

concepts.title: Worker threads
concepts.definition: Workers can run CPU-heavy JavaScript outside the request thread, with messaging and resource costs.

concepts.title: Cluster
concepts.definition: Cluster supports multiple Node processes; process-local state is not a shared authoritative database.

concepts.title: Event loop
concepts.definition: Node coordinates asynchronous work through runtime phases and queues; expensive synchronous work blocks progress.

concepts.title: Async programming
concepts.definition: Handle ordering, failures, bounded concurrency, and cleanup explicitly.

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.definition: Separate expected domain errors from unexpected runtime failures and preserve useful diagnostic context.

concepts.title: Performance
concepts.definition: Profile latency, CPU, allocation, and resource contention with a representative workload.

concepts.title: Security
concepts.definition: Constrain inputs, file paths, commands, secrets, dependency access, and network capabilities.

concepts.title: Testing
concepts.definition: Exercise contracts with unit, integration, and real-network checks appropriate to the boundary.

concepts.title: Server creation
concepts.definition: Create an application, mount middleware and routes, then listen through an HTTP server with a controlled lifecycle.

concepts.title: Routing
concepts.definition: Routing selects handlers by method and path; unknown API paths must not silently become frontend HTML.

concepts.title: Middleware
concepts.definition: Middleware can inspect, transform, terminate, or delegate a request; order defines behavior.

concepts.title: Request/response
concepts.definition: Requests contain untrusted inputs; responses implement the API status, headers, and representation contract.

concepts.title: Controllers
concepts.definition: Controllers adapt HTTP details to validated service inputs and domain outcomes.

concepts.title: Services
concepts.definition: Services own domain rules that should not depend unnecessarily on the HTTP transport.

concepts.title: REST APIs
concepts.definition: REST uses resources and representations with coherent HTTP semantics and operational contracts.

concepts.title: Validation
concepts.definition: Validate types, lengths, allowed fields, ranges, and relationships before trusted use.

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.definition: Centralize safe client errors while retaining server diagnostic evidence; Express 5 forwards rejected returned Promises.

concepts.title: Authentication
concepts.definition: Resolve identity from trusted credentials rather than client-supplied role or owner fields.

concepts.title: Authorization
concepts.definition: Every read and write must enforce the authenticated caller's permission for the resource.

concepts.title: Cookies
concepts.definition: Cookies are browser-managed values with scope and security attributes; they can accompany cross-site requests under applicable rules.

concepts.title: Sessions
concepts.definition: Sessions connect credentials to server-side authority with expiration and revocation.

concepts.title: File uploads
concepts.definition: Limit size and count, validate content, isolate storage, and avoid trusting original filenames or declared MIME type.

concepts.title: Pagination
concepts.definition: Bound lists and define stable ordering and a cursor or offset contract.

concepts.title: Filtering
concepts.definition: Allowlist supported predicates and normalize values rather than accepting arbitrary query operators.

concepts.title: Sorting
concepts.definition: Allowlist fields and directions with a stable tie-breaker when needed.

concepts.title: Searching
concepts.definition: Specify matching behavior and bound query cost; avoid uncontrolled patterns or arbitrary regular expressions.

concepts.title: Rate limiting
concepts.definition: Choose keys and scope; a process-local limiter is not a consistent global limit across instances.

concepts.title: Logging
concepts.definition: Record useful request context and safe errors while redacting secrets and sensitive payloads.

concepts.title: Security
concepts.definition: Layer input constraints, identity, authorization, origin defenses, safe headers, and operational limits.

concepts.title: API architecture
concepts.definition: Separate transport, domain behavior, and persistence so tests can target the relevant contract.

concepts.title: Production structure
concepts.definition: Include startup validation, repeatable builds, safe error behavior, monitoring, graceful shutdown, and deployment requirements.

concepts.title: Documents
concepts.definition: Documents hold structured fields and nested values; model them around access and ownership patterns.

concepts.title: Collections
concepts.definition: Collections group documents and can have validation rules and indexes.

concepts.title: BSON
concepts.definition: BSON is MongoDB's binary representation with types beyond JSON, including ObjectId and dates.

concepts.title: CRUD
concepts.definition: Create, read, update, and delete must preserve domain constraints and caller scope.

concepts.title: Operators
concepts.definition: Operators express matching and updates; build permitted expressions rather than accepting arbitrary input operators.

concepts.title: Querying
concepts.definition: A query selects documents according to predicates, available indexes, and execution behavior.

concepts.title: Projection
concepts.definition: Projection limits fields returned; it can reduce transfer and prevent accidental disclosure.

concepts.title: Sorting
concepts.definition: Sort determines order; include a tie-breaker when pagination requires stable identity.

concepts.title: Pagination
concepts.definition: Cursor pagination continues from a defined position; offset pagination can shift when earlier rows change.

concepts.title: Indexes
concepts.definition: Indexes support selected access patterns and enforce uniqueness when configured; they add write and storage cost.

concepts.title: Aggregation
concepts.definition: A pipeline transforms a stream of documents through ordered stages such as match, group, and project.

concepts.title: Transactions
concepts.definition: Multi-document transactions coordinate invariants when one atomic document operation cannot express them; deployment support matters.

concepts.title: Schema design
concepts.definition: Define required types and relationships despite flexible storage; schema evolution needs intentional migration.

concepts.title: Data modeling
concepts.definition: Embedding and references trade read locality, growth, duplication, and independent lifecycle.

concepts.title: Replication
concepts.definition: Replica sets provide multiple copies and failover behavior; read/write concern choices affect guarantees.

concepts.title: Performance
concepts.definition: Inspect explain plans and representative data; document and query shapes matter more than a database label.

concepts.title: Connection
concepts.definition: Connect deliberately, validate configuration, and manage startup failure and shutdown.

concepts.title: Schema
concepts.definition: A schema describes casting, defaults, validation, middleware, and model behavior; it is distinct from database validation.

concepts.title: Models
concepts.definition: Models provide collection operations built from a schema and connection.

concepts.title: Validation
concepts.definition: Validation rejects selected invalid values; update validation has specific supported operators and context rules.

concepts.title: Middleware
concepts.definition: Middleware surrounds selected operations; document and query middleware have different this and lifecycle behavior.

concepts.title: Methods
concepts.definition: Document methods attach behavior to a hydrated document; avoid arrows when document this is required.

concepts.title: Statics
concepts.definition: Statics expose model-level behavior such as a carefully scoped query helper.

concepts.title: Virtuals
concepts.definition: Virtuals compute or expose values without ordinary persisted fields; serialization options affect visibility.

concepts.title: Populate
concepts.definition: Populate resolves references through additional query behavior; bound cost and avoid leaking fields.

concepts.title: References
concepts.definition: References connect identities but do not automatically provide foreign-key enforcement.

concepts.title: Transactions
concepts.definition: Use a supported deployment and shared session for coordinated operations; avoid unsupported parallel transaction patterns.

concepts.title: Indexes
concepts.definition: Schema index declarations describe desired indexes; verify actual database creation and migrations.

concepts.title: Aggregation
concepts.definition: Aggregation operates through pipeline semantics that differ from hydrated-document methods and query casting.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: Relational data is represented through relations with explicit columns and constraints; SQL expresses operations over these sets.

concepts.title: MySQL
concepts.definition: MySQL is a relational database with engine and version-specific capabilities; select the actual documentation and isolation contract.

concepts.title: PostgreSQL
concepts.definition: PostgreSQL supports relational queries, constraints, transactions, and additional types; syntax can differ from MySQL.

concepts.title: CRUD
concepts.definition: Insert, select, update, and delete should use parameters and enforce caller scope.

concepts.title: Joins
concepts.definition: Joins combine rows according to predicates; one-to-many relationships can multiply rows.

concepts.title: Subqueries
concepts.definition: Subqueries supply values or relations to another query; correlated work and plans can affect performance.

concepts.title: CTE
concepts.definition: A common table expression names a query result within a statement; optimization behavior is database-dependent.

concepts.title: Window functions
concepts.definition: Window functions calculate across related rows while retaining individual rows, such as rank or running totals.

concepts.title: Indexes
concepts.definition: Indexes accelerate selected lookups and ordering while adding write and storage cost.

concepts.title: Transactions
concepts.definition: Transactions group operations with defined isolation behavior; atomicity does not mean all concurrent anomalies disappear.

concepts.title: Constraints
concepts.definition: Primary keys, unique, foreign keys, not-null, and check constraints protect selected invariants in the database.

concepts.title: Normalization
concepts.definition: Normalization reduces problematic redundancy; deliberate denormalization needs update and consistency rules.

concepts.title: Query optimization
concepts.definition: Inspect explain plans with representative cardinality, predicates, ordering, and constraints.

concepts.title: Fundamentals
concepts.definition: Redis provides data structures with operational persistence and replication choices; memory is not automatically durable authority.

concepts.title: Caching
concepts.definition: A cache reuses derived values with explicit scope, freshness, expiration, and invalidation.

concepts.title: Sessions
concepts.definition: Shared session storage can coordinate identity across instances when expiration, revocation, and availability rules are defined.

concepts.title: Pub/Sub
concepts.definition: Pub/Sub delivers to current subscribers and is not a durable replayable queue for disconnected consumers.

concepts.title: Rate limiting
concepts.definition: Atomic shared counters or scripts can implement a chosen limit policy; define windows, keys, and failure mode.

concepts.title: Queues
concepts.definition: Durable job systems need acknowledgement, retry, idempotency, and recovery, beyond merely pushing a list value.

concepts.title: Distributed locks
concepts.definition: Locks have expiry and ownership constraints; stale holders may need fencing enforced by the protected resource.

concepts.title: Cloud fundamentals
concepts.definition: Cloud platforms offer managed resources under explicit availability, pricing, and responsibility models.

concepts.title: Deployment architecture
concepts.definition: Map clients, compute, stores, networks, secrets, and failure boundaries before selecting a service.

concepts.title: Compute
concepts.definition: Compute runs workloads under resource limits and lifecycle rules, whether instances, containers, or functions.

concepts.title: Storage
concepts.definition: Object, block, and filesystem storage have different access and durability contracts.

concepts.title: Databases
concepts.definition: Managed databases reduce some operating work, while schema, queries, permissions, and recovery remain application responsibilities.

concepts.title: CDN
concepts.definition: A CDN distributes cacheable content closer to clients; private data and invalidation need intentional policies.

concepts.title: DNS
concepts.definition: DNS directs names to services with propagation and caching behavior relevant to migrations.

concepts.title: Environment management
concepts.definition: Separate development, test, and production identities, configuration, and data.

concepts.title: Secrets
concepts.definition: Provide credentials through a controlled secret mechanism, with least privilege and rotation.

concepts.title: Scaling
concepts.definition: Scale the measured bottleneck while accounting for shared-state, connection, and dependency limits.

concepts.title: Clean code
concepts.definition: Names, small coherent contracts, explicit boundaries, and readable control flow make change easier to assess.

concepts.title: SOLID
concepts.definition: SOLID principles describe responsibility and substitutability concerns; applying them mechanically can overcomplicate small systems.

concepts.title: DRY
concepts.definition: Remove duplicated knowledge whose inconsistent evolution would cause bugs; similar-looking code can have different reasons to change.

concepts.title: KISS
concepts.definition: Prefer a simple sufficient model that makes the important behavior visible.

concepts.title: YAGNI
concepts.definition: Delay speculative capabilities until a real requirement justifies their cost.

concepts.title: Design patterns
concepts.definition: Patterns name recurring solutions and tradeoffs; choose them for a concrete problem rather than a diagram collection.

concepts.title: Architecture patterns
concepts.definition: Architectural styles organize dependency and deployment boundaries under specific constraints.

concepts.title: Layered architecture
concepts.definition: Layers separate transport, domain, and persistence responsibilities when this clarifies ownership.

concepts.title: MVC
concepts.definition: MVC separates model, view, and controller roles, though framework interpretations vary.

concepts.title: Clean architecture
concepts.definition: Clean architecture directs dependencies toward domain behavior and uses adapters around external systems.

concepts.title: Dependency injection
concepts.definition: Pass dependencies explicitly so authority, failure behavior, and test boundaries are visible.

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.definition: Translate errors at meaningful boundaries without losing diagnostic context or exposing secrets.

concepts.title: Logging
concepts.definition: Logs record contextual events; structured fields help query them and redaction prevents sensitive disclosure.

concepts.title: Observability
concepts.definition: Logs, metrics, and traces provide evidence about internal behavior; useful signals are tied to concrete questions.

concepts.title: Documentation
concepts.definition: Document contracts, decisions, setup, limitations, and verification so another developer can act without guessing.

concepts.title: Scalability
concepts.definition: Scalability is the ability to support a changing workload under stated resource and performance constraints.

concepts.title: Availability
concepts.definition: Availability describes whether useful service is accessible under defined failure conditions.

concepts.title: Reliability
concepts.definition: Reliability concerns correct operation over time, including detection, recovery, and preserved invariants.

concepts.title: Load balancing
concepts.definition: Load balancers distribute requests among eligible targets; health and connection behavior affect outcomes.

concepts.title: Caching
concepts.definition: Caching reuses representations under scope and freshness rules; invalidation and stampede behavior matter.

concepts.title: Database scaling
concepts.definition: Improve schema, queries, indexes, and workload before choosing replication or partitioning complexity.

concepts.title: Replication
concepts.definition: Replicas copy data with lag and failure behavior; reads need consistency requirements.

concepts.title: Sharding
concepts.definition: Sharding partitions data and introduces routing, balancing, hotspot, and cross-partition concerns.

concepts.title: Queues
concepts.definition: Queues decouple work with acknowledgment, retry, backpressure, and idempotency contracts.

concepts.title: Pub/Sub
concepts.definition: Publish/subscribe routes events to interested consumers; durability depends on the chosen system and configuration.

concepts.title: CDN
concepts.definition: CDNs distribute reusable content and require cache-key, invalidation, and privacy policies.

concepts.title: Rate limiting
concepts.definition: A limiter constrains work under explicit identity, window, deployment scope, and failure behavior.

concepts.title: CAP theorem
concepts.definition: During a network partition, a distributed system cannot guarantee both linearizable consistency and availability in the theorem's sense.

concepts.title: Consistency
concepts.definition: Consistency models describe which observations are permitted; choose requirements for each operation.

concepts.title: Distributed systems
concepts.definition: Multiple nodes communicate under delay, failure, and partial knowledge; local success is not a global guarantee.

concepts.title: High-level design
concepts.definition: High-level design identifies components, data flow, scale assumptions, and failure boundaries.

concepts.title: Low-level design
concepts.definition: Low-level design describes data models, interfaces, states, algorithms, and invariants inside those components.

concepts.title: REST
concepts.definition: REST organizes interaction around resources and representations; use coherent HTTP semantics rather than arbitrary action names.

concepts.title: GraphQL
concepts.definition: GraphQL uses a typed schema and selection sets; resolvers still need authorization, cost bounds, and error contracts.

concepts.title: HTTP methods
concepts.definition: Methods have semantics such as retrieval, replacement, and partial update; choose them consistently.

concepts.title: Status codes
concepts.definition: Status codes describe response outcomes; preserve distinctions clients need for recovery.

concepts.title: Headers
concepts.definition: Headers carry representation, caching, authentication, and other protocol metadata.

concepts.title: Authentication
concepts.definition: Authentication establishes the caller's trusted identity from accepted credentials.

concepts.title: Authorization
concepts.definition: Authorization establishes whether that caller may perform this operation on this resource.

concepts.title: Pagination
concepts.definition: Lists need bounded sizes and a stable continuation or offset contract.

concepts.title: Filtering
concepts.definition: Supported filter fields and operators should be explicit and validated.

concepts.title: Sorting
concepts.definition: Document ordering, allowed fields, and tie-breakers rather than accepting arbitrary expressions.

concepts.title: Versioning
concepts.definition: Versioning manages incompatible contract changes; keep compatibility policy visible to consumers.

concepts.title: Validation
concepts.definition: Validate runtime shape, types, ranges, allowed fields, and domain relationships.

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.definition: Return safe structured errors with a stable code and useful message; preserve server diagnostic context separately.

concepts.title: Rate limiting
concepts.definition: Define caller identity, window policy, distributed scope, and recovery guidance.

concepts.title: API documentation
concepts.definition: Document authentication, inputs, outputs, errors, limits, and examples for actual implemented behavior.

concepts.title: OpenAPI / Swagger
concepts.definition: OpenAPI describes HTTP contracts; Swagger is a family of tools around API descriptions rather than another protocol.

concepts.title: Password hashing
concepts.definition: Store a password-specific salted verifier with suitable cost, not reversible plaintext encryption.

concepts.title: bcrypt
concepts.definition: bcrypt is a password-hashing option with cost and input-length considerations; follow current guidance for new systems.

concepts.title: JWT
concepts.definition: A signed JWT provides integrity for claims, not confidentiality; validate issuer, audience, algorithm, and expiry.

concepts.title: Access tokens
concepts.definition: Access credentials authorize a bounded scope and lifetime; keep exposure and revocation needs explicit.

concepts.title: Refresh tokens
concepts.definition: Refresh credentials renew access and need protected storage, rotation, reuse detection, and revocation policy.

concepts.title: Cookies
concepts.definition: Cookie attributes control scope and handling; HttpOnly blocks ordinary script reads but does not stop all authenticated abuse.

concepts.title: Sessions
concepts.definition: Server-side sessions support expiry and revocation; store only necessary authority and enforce expiry during lookup.

concepts.title: OAuth
concepts.definition: OAuth delegates access under a protocol; identity login usually also needs an appropriate identity layer such as OpenID Connect.

concepts.title: RBAC
concepts.definition: Role-based permissions group allowed actions; object ownership and tenant scope still need enforcement.

concepts.title: CORS
concepts.definition: CORS controls browser cross-origin response access; it is not API authentication and does not stop non-browser callers.

concepts.title: CSRF
concepts.definition: Cookie-authenticated writes need cross-site request defenses such as suitable tokens, origin checks, and SameSite policy.

concepts.title: XSS
concepts.definition: Untrusted content executed in the page can act with the page's privileges; render data safely and constrain script execution.

concepts.title: SQL injection
concepts.definition: Parameterized queries separate values from SQL structure; dynamic identifiers require allowlists.

concepts.title: NoSQL injection
concepts.definition: Construct permitted query predicates from validated scalars instead of accepting arbitrary operator objects.

concepts.title: Rate limiting
concepts.definition: Limit abuse according to a defined identity and deployment scope; consider cost and recovery as well as request count.

concepts.title: Helmet
concepts.definition: Helmet sets security-related HTTP headers, but does not replace input validation or authorization.

concepts.title: Secure headers
concepts.definition: Headers can constrain browser capabilities and content interpretation; configure them for the actual deployment.

concepts.title: Secrets
concepts.definition: Keep secrets out of source, logs, browser bundles, and artifacts; rotate compromised credentials.

concepts.title: OWASP
concepts.definition: OWASP offers threat-focused guidance; use it to evaluate concrete application boundaries.

concepts.title: Security best practices
concepts.definition: Define assets, threats, trusted identities, permitted operations, and recovery; verify them with adversarial cases.

concepts.title: WebSockets
concepts.definition: WebSockets provide bidirectional messages over a long-lived connection; application protocols still define identity and delivery.

concepts.title: Socket.IO
concepts.definition: Socket.IO adds its own protocol, reconnection, rooms, and acknowledgements; it is not wire-compatible with plain WebSocket clients.

concepts.title: Server-Sent Events
concepts.definition: SSE streams server-to-client events over HTTP; EventSource handles connection behavior while replay needs application design.

concepts.title: Notifications
concepts.definition: Notifications need ownership, stable event ids, read state, and a catch-up mechanism after disconnect.

concepts.title: Chat architecture
concepts.definition: Chat combines durable messages, authorized rooms, delivery acknowledgements, ordering, and reconnect recovery.

concepts.title: Presence
concepts.definition: Presence is typically an expiring observation of connectivity, not a durable statement that someone is actively reading.

concepts.title: Real-time dashboards
concepts.definition: Dashboards need bounded update frequency, backpressure, and a consistent initial snapshot or replay position.

concepts.title: Unit testing
concepts.definition: A unit check exercises a small behavioral contract with controlled inputs and an independent expected outcome.

concepts.title: Integration testing
concepts.definition: Integration checks exercise boundaries between real components such as HTTP parsing and persistence.

concepts.title: API testing
concepts.definition: API checks verify identity, input, status, representation, ownership, and failure behavior.

concepts.title: Component testing
concepts.definition: Component checks exercise visible interaction and state without relying unnecessarily on implementation structure.

concepts.title: End-to-end testing
concepts.definition: Browser workflows exercise important user paths through realistic routing, focus, network, and persistence.

concepts.title: Jest
concepts.definition: Jest supplies a test runner and mocking ecosystem; configuration and environments affect module behavior.

concepts.title: Vitest
concepts.definition: Vitest integrates with Vite-oriented projects and offers runner and mocking capabilities.

concepts.title: React Testing Library
concepts.definition: Testing Library encourages user-oriented queries and interaction rather than component internals.

concepts.title: Supertest
concepts.definition: Supertest drives HTTP applications through request assertions; its boundary scope must still be stated.

concepts.title: Playwright
concepts.definition: Playwright automates real browsers with locators, assertions, traces, and workflow tools.

concepts.title: Cypress
concepts.definition: Cypress offers browser-oriented end-to-end and component testing with its own execution model.

concepts.title: Linux
concepts.definition: Linux provides process, filesystem, permission, networking, and service primitives commonly used in deployments.

concepts.title: Shell
concepts.definition: Shell commands operate on files and processes; quoting and argument boundaries prevent accidental interpretation.

concepts.title: Environment variables
concepts.definition: Validate configuration at startup and keep secrets separate from source and images.

concepts.title: Docker
concepts.definition: Docker packages applications with runtime dependencies using images and managed containers.

concepts.title: Docker Compose
concepts.definition: Compose defines a multi-service application for a chosen environment; local convenience is not a complete production plan.

concepts.title: Images
concepts.definition: Images contain filesystem layers and runtime metadata; build reproducibly and avoid baking secrets into layers.

concepts.title: Containers
concepts.definition: Containers are isolated processes sharing host infrastructure, not complete independent virtual machines.

concepts.title: Volumes
concepts.definition: Volumes persist data beyond a container lifecycle and need backup and restore procedures.

concepts.title: Networks
concepts.definition: Container networks define communication paths; avoid exposing internal databases unnecessarily.

concepts.title: CI/CD
concepts.definition: CI validates proposed changes; delivery prepares releases; deployment changes a running environment under a release policy.

concepts.title: GitHub Actions
concepts.definition: Actions workflows coordinate jobs with explicit triggers, inputs, and permissions.

concepts.title: Nginx
concepts.definition: Nginx can serve static resources and reverse-proxy HTTP; forwarded-header and timeout configuration need care.

concepts.title: Reverse proxy
concepts.definition: A proxy sits between clients and services and can handle routing, TLS, limits, or static assets.

concepts.title: SSL/TLS
concepts.definition: TLS encrypts transport and authenticates endpoints; SSL is historical terminology for obsolete predecessor protocols.

concepts.title: Deployment
concepts.definition: Deployment includes configuration, migrations, health, rollback, and dependency availability.

concepts.title: Monitoring
concepts.definition: Monitoring observes signals and actionable conditions; a reachable process is not necessarily ready to serve.

concepts.title: Logging
concepts.definition: Structured logs support diagnosis while preserving secrecy and limiting volume.
